system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Occlusion attribution of MVFA's detection branch as pseudo-masks for its segmentation branch
SUMMARY: Train the detection branch on image-level labels, then mark as anomalous the patches whose replacement by their nearest normal-bank feature most reduces the detection branch's image score, and use these attribution maps as segmentation targets.
HYPOTHESIS: Occlusion-attribution pseudo-masks from the image-label-trained detection branch achieve at least 8 points higher Dice against true masks than nearest-neighbour pseudo-masks on at least two of the three masked datasets, and MVFA trained on them recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC.
RATIONALE: The veto idea uses the detection branch's map as a second opinion. By analogy with counterfactual explanation in weakly supervised localisation, the detection branch, trained with reliable image labels on all six datasets, implicitly knows which patches make an image abnormal: replacing such a patch by its closest normal counterpart should lower the image score. This counterfactual occlusion gives a causal attribution rather than a correlational map, uses only components that MVFA already has (det_adapters and a normal bank), and directly targets the problem's question of what image-level labels can teach the segmentation branch.
METHOD: 1) Stage 1: train det_adapters only (train_zero.py, seg loss off) on all six sources, 20 epochs, selected on source-validation image AUROC. 2) For each abnormal source image: features F per level; for each patch p, F_p' = F with patch p replaced by its nearest neighbour in the dataset's normal bank at each level; attribution a_p = score(F) - score(F_p') with score the det branch's mean-pooled anomaly output (batched over patches: 289 forward passes of the adapters only, CLIP features cached). 3) Pseudo-mask = a_p > 99th percentile of a on normal source-validation images (where attributions should be small). 4) Stage 2: train seg branch on these masks with Focal + Dice; det branch continues. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; NN pseudo-masks; occlusion pseudo-masks; Grad-CAM of the det branch (cheaper attribution baseline). Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if occlusion masks do not beat NN pseudo-masks by 8 Dice points on two masked datasets or do not beat Grad-CAM.

Idea B:
TITLE: Dawid-Skene fusion of MVFA-internal pseudo-label sources with per-dataset reliabilities
SUMMARY: Treat the nearest-neighbour rule, the detection-branch map and the zero-shot text map as three noisy annotators of each patch, and estimate each annotator's sensitivity and specificity per source dataset with the Dawid-Skene EM algorithm, constrained by image labels, to obtain posterior pseudo-masks.
HYPOTHESIS: Dawid-Skene posteriors from three MVFA-internal sources reach at least 6 points higher pseudo-mask Dice than the best single source on each masked dataset, the estimated per-source reliabilities rank the sources in the same order as their true Dice on masked datasets, and MVFA trained on the posteriors recovers at least 92% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC.
RATIONALE: The veto parent combines two views with a fixed agreement rule. By analogy with crowdsourced labelling, where several unreliable annotators are combined by estimating each one's error rates without ground truth (Dawid-Skene), MVFA offers several independent patch-level signals whose reliability probably differs by modality: feature distance may work on MRI, the detection map on OCT. EM estimates these reliabilities per dataset from agreement patterns, with image labels as a hard constraint (normal images contain no anomalous patch), so the fusion adapts to each dataset instead of using one rule everywhere.
METHOD: 1) Sources per abnormal and normal source image: NN rule (binary), detection-branch top-20% map (from a det-only stage-1 model), frozen-CLIP zero-shot map thresholded at its source-validation 99th percentile on normals. 2) Dawid-Skene with binary labels per patch, per dataset: parameters (sens_j, spec_j) for each source j and prior pi; EM for 50 iterations; patches of normal images fixed to label 0 (provides specificity estimates directly). 3) Posterior P(y_p = 1); targets = posterior > 0.5, ignore 0.3-0.7. 4) Stage 2: train MVFA with masked Focal + Dice. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; each single source; majority vote; Dawid-Skene posterior. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice per dataset, rank correlation between estimated and true source reliability, trained pixel AUROC, Dice. Falsified if Dawid-Skene does not beat the best single source by 6 Dice points or majority vote by 2.

Respond in exactly this format:

CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
